title: French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future : A Report
content:
This past week, thousands of teenagers have taken the streets of France, clashing with police as they demonstrate against the deplorable conditions in their high schools and a rapidly collapsing future. This is a promising sign, shifting attention from the seemingly unstoppable rise of the extreme right to the question of what people can do on a grassroots basis to defend themselves. Our correspondents in Paris explore the situation in detail.







Another unprecedented summer of record 

heatwaves

, 

droughts

, and 

wildfires

 throughout Europe underlines the desperate situation we are all facing today, while politicians of all stripes and their techno-industrial sponsors continue to turn a blind eye, forcing us down the path to catastrophe in the name of progress.




Hoping to turn the page on these environmental disasters, the French government has hurriedly shifted focus to other priorities. The coming months represent a crucial transition for Emmanuel Macron and his government, as they will bring Macron’s second term to a close, opening a new political era in France. Candidates are already battling to succeed Macron in power at the beginning of May 2027.

title: "Never Again": Czechoslovakian Hardcore in the Syrian Civil War
content:
In the following narrative, anarchists who participated as internationalist volunteers in the fight to defend Rojava against the Islamic State describe the role that the anti-militarist song “Už Nikdy” (“Never Again”) by the Czechoslovakian hardcore band Kritická Situace played in their experience.




This text is adapted from the newest issue of the anarchist hardcore publication 

Inside Front

.

 We share it here to explore the importance of revolutionary music and culture in social movements. 

The personal is geopolitical.




These events took place in March 2019, near the end of the fight against the Islamic State. At that time, the Turkish army and its Syrian proxies had brutally seized the majority-Kurdish district of Afrin in northwest Syria, and Donald Trump was 

signaling

 that he would permit them to attack the rest of Rojava as well. At the same time, the Islamic State still controlled territory in Deir Ezzor in the southeast, where the final battles took place at al-Baghuz Fawqani.




As soon as the Islamic State was defeated, the United States government gave Turkey the green light to 

butcher

 those who had defeated it. In 2024, 

Turkish-backed forces

 came to power in Syria, creating 

new challenges

 for the multiethnic revolutionary experiment in Rojava. Nonetheless, the fight for free life continues—in Rojava and the 

rest

 of Syria, in 

Turkey
